matchups.analysis: Doakes22 is walking out of this at 52% and ESPN's projecting a 3.3-point squeaker (125.5 to 122.2), which means this thing is still completely up for grabs with both rosters still loaded with studs on the bench. You've got the firepower to pull this off with Saquon, Lamar, and Brock Bowers still waiting to go, but kconley5's got an equally stacked remaining slate with Bijan, Henry, and Drake Maye ready to punch back—this is a proper matchup, not a coronation. Neither of you made any meaningful lineup mistakes, so whoever's studs decide to show up and whoever's guys underperform is going to be the difference, and right now ESPN thinks it's basically a coin flip on which side that'll be.

ESPNFAN6437471416's got this locked at 61% win probability with ESPN projecting 122.8 final—that's a 21.8-point cushion over SteelerFan9828's 101.0, which basically means you're coasting home assuming your studs (Cook, Wilson, Purdy, 49ers D) show up with the rest of your nine starters still waiting in the wings. SteelerFan's got nine starters left too and is somehow still projected to lose by nearly 22 despite the fact that nobody's played yet, which tells you everything about how badly you both whiffed on roster construction—but at least ESPNFAN's got the better lineup by a country mile. The math is simple: Amon-Ra and Breece Hall need to go absolutely nuclear while half of your receiving corps needs to implode just to make this competitive, and ESPN's saying that's only happening 39% of the time. SteelerFan, you're basically asking for ceiling games across the board to avoid getting run off the field by a guy whose biggest advantage is just having better talent on the roster—that's not a path to victory, that's desperation.

RGM2215's looking at a 37-point deficit with ESPN projecting 94.1 final versus espnfan7338848211's 131.3—win probability says 31% for RGM, which is basically a polite way of saying this is over. RGM still has nine starters to play which technically keeps them alive, but they're going to need Christian McCaffrey and Dak Prescott both going full ceiling mode while espnfan7338848211's stack of Ja'Marr Chase, Kenneth Walker III, and D'Andre Swift stays within projections—ESPN's got espnfan winning this at 69% and that gap's only widening as Sunday unfolds. Neither manager made a meaningful lineup mistake, so this is purely a roster construction story: one team just built significantly better at the skill positions and it shows in the projections, which is the most brutal type of loss because you can't even blame yourself for leaving points on the bench.

ESPNfan83795608 and 82Cole47 are basically tied at the starting line here—both sitting at 121-128 projected with nine starters left to play and win probabilities that are basically a coin flip, so this thing won't be decided until the final kicker limps off the field. Neither one of you made any lineup mistakes to roast, which is genuinely shocking after watching some of these matchups this week, so instead you're just gonna live and die by whether your studs show up or your opponent's don't. ESPNfan's got Smith-Njigba and Olave in there to carry weight, while Cole's banking on Gibbs and Allen to keep pace, but with everyone still in play and ESPN practically begging for a tiebreaker, this is legitimately a toss-up—may the fantasy gods favor whoever remembered to actually set their lineup instead of sleepwalking through Sunday.

ESPN88256878's got the 46% win probability and a 7.1-point projection deficit (108.3 to 115.4), which means Eric Brotmann's sitting in the driver's seat even though both of you are basically waiting for your entire rosters to play out. Still, you've got enough time to flip this if your studs show up and his underperform, so this thing's legitimately not over.
